# Concept: Cognitive Ledger

The cognitive ledger is a personal knowledge management system that stores structured facts, preferences, goals, and open loops as searchable notes.

## Context

Unlike a general note-taking tool, the cognitive ledger categorises notes by type (facts, preferences, goals, concepts, open loops).
Retrieval is the core capability: the ledger can answer questions by searching and ranking relevant notes.
The system is designed to be an external memory that complements natural human cognition.
The cognitive-ledger project is Alex's implementation of this concept using Python.

candidate.statement: Spaced repetition is a learning technique that schedules reviews of information at increasing intervals to maximise long-term retention.
candidate.body:
# Concept: Spaced Repetition

## Statement

Spaced repetition is a learning technique that schedules reviews of information at increasing intervals to maximise long-term retention.

## Context

The core idea is that memory decays over time following the Ebbinghaus forgetting curve.
By reviewing information just before it is forgotten, retention is reinforced efficiently.
Anki is the most widely used spaced repetition software, using a flashcard model.
Alex uses spaced repetition for language vocabulary and technical concepts.

## Links

- [[pref__learning_style]]
- [[concept__zettelkasten]]
candidate.snippet: Spaced repetition is a learning technique that schedules reviews of information at increasing intervals to maximise long-term retention.

candidate.body:
# Concept: Zettelkasten Method

## Statement

The Zettelkasten method is a knowledge management system based on atomic notes linked together into a web of ideas.

## Context

Developed by sociologist Niklas Luhmann, who used it to write dozens of books.
Each note (Zettel) contains a single idea and links to related notes.
The value emerges from the connections between notes, not individual notes in isolation.
Obsidian implements a digital Zettelkasten through markdown files and wiki-style links.

## Links

- [[pref__note_taking_tool]]
- [[concept__spaced_repetition]]
candidate.snippet: The Zettelkasten method is a knowledge management system based on atomic notes linked together into a web of ideas.
